title: Military Service Hold Extensions Booked by the Servicemember — Hardship and Protective Holds
content:
## Terms

Under Hardship and Protective Holds, a running Military Service Hold may be extended up to the tier's maximum number of extensions, each extension adding the days the service extension adds to the hold's end date; a running Long-Term Hardship Hold is extended under its own extension rule, and a running hold of any other tier may be extended at the consumer's request up to the tier's maximum number of extensions, each extension adding the tier's extension days to its end date.

Because the protection rests on the servicemember's own active-duty orders, the extension is the servicemember's own election: once updated orders are on record and the request falls inside the tier's extension window, the servicemember books it in person through the self-service portal, and the desk tells the servicemember the days the service extension adds.

For a Military Service Hold, as for a hold of every other tier, the hold's current end date is the end date on record: the start date plus the initial hold days minus 1, plus the days each extension already granted added, counted in calendar days with the last day included, and the hold completes its term on that date.

The servicemember's own booking through the portal is the decision on a Military Service Hold extension and takes effect the day it is made; a Long-Term Hardship Hold extension is decided under its own extension rule, and an extension of a hold of any other tier is decided within the tier's extension decision days, counted as business days.

## Who does what

| Party | Part in the extension |
|---|---|
| Servicemember | Elects the extension and books it in person through the self-service portal, once updated orders are on record and the request falls inside the tier's extension window |
| Desk | Tells the servicemember the days the service extension adds |
| Effect | The booking is the decision and takes effect the day it is made |

| Hold of another tier | Extension and decision |
|---|---|
| Long-Term Hardship Hold | Extended and decided under its own extension rule |
| Any other tier | Extended at the consumer's request up to the tier's maximum number of extensions, each adding the tier's extension days to its end date; decided within the tier's extension decision days, counted as business days |

## Tool card: `extend_service_hold_a0a57648`

**Capability.** The servicemember extends their own running Military Service Hold through the self-service portal on the active-duty orders already on file. One call books one extension: it records the extension in the hold history with today's date, the extension's sequence number and the days added, and moves the hold's end date on record — its last covered day — forward by those days, counting the extension count up by one. The hold stays active. On success the servicemember and the desk see the new last day of the hold and the extension in its history.

**How it is invoked.** This is the servicemember's own tool. The agent unlocks `extend_service_hold_a0a57648` and hands it over; the customer themselves — the servicemember — runs it in person through the portal.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `hold_id` | The hold reference number of the servicemember's running Military Service Hold, which the agent reads from the hardship hold lookup and gives to the servicemember | Identifier |
| `extension_days` | The days the extension adds, in calendar days, that the agent tells the servicemember; the new last day of the hold is the current last day plus this many days | Whole number of at least 1, no decimals |

**Return.** A dictionary rendered as text with `extension_ref` (the reference of the recorded extension), `hold_id`, `extension_number` (which extension of the hold this is), `days_added` (calendar days), `previous_end_date` (YYYY-MM-DD), `new_end_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, the hold's new last covered day) and `status`, always `extended` when the extension is booked.

**Input and receipt (hypothetical).** On a hold whose last covered day is 30 June, a booking with `extension_days` of 60 returns a `new_end_date` of 29 August.
